In [[type theory]], a discipline within [[mathematical logic]], '''containers''' are abstractions which permit various "collection types", such as [[list (computing)|lists]] and [[tree (data structure)|trees]], to be represented in a uniform way. A ([[unary operation|unary]]) container is defined by a type of ''shapes'' S and a type family of ''positions'' P, indexed by S. The ''extension'' of a container is a family of dependent pairs consisting of a shape (of type S) and a function from positions of that shape to the element type. Containers can be seen as [[canonical form]]s (standard form) for collection types.<ref name='containers'>{{cite journal |author1=Michael Abbott |author2=Thorsten Altenkirch |author3=Neil Ghani |year=2005 |title=Containers: Constructing strictly positive types  |journal=Theoretical Computer Science |volume=342 |issue=1 |pages=3–27 |doi=10.1016/j.tcs.2005.06.002|doi-access=free |citeseerx=10.1.1.166.34 }}</ref>

For lists, the shape type is the [[natural number]]s (including zero). The corresponding position types are the types of natural numbers less than the shape, for each shape.

For trees, the shape type is the type of trees of units (that is, trees with no information in them, just structure). The corresponding position types are isomorphic to the types of valid paths from the root to particular nodes on the shape, for each shape.

Note that the natural numbers are [[Isomorphism|isomorphic]] to lists of units. In general the shape type will always be isomorphic to the original non-generic container type family (list, tree etc.) applied to unit.

One of the main motivations for introducing the notion of containers is to support [[generic programming]] in a [[dependent type|dependently typed]] setting.<ref name='containers'/>

== Categorical aspects ==
The extension of a container is an [[endofunctor]]. It takes a function <code>g</code> to
: <math>\lambda(s,f).(s,g\circ f)</math>
This is equivalent to the familiar <code>map g</code> in the case of lists, and does something similar for other containers.

Containers form a [[category (mathematics)|category]] in which a morphism from <math>S \triangleleft P</math> to <math>T \triangleleft Q</math> is a function <math>u \colon S \to T</math> on shapes together with functions <math>h_s \colon Q\,(u\,s) \to P\,s</math> mapping positions ''backwards''; it acts on extensions by <math>\lambda(s,f).(u\,s,\, f \circ h_s)</math>. Extension is a [[Full and faithful functors|full and faithful]] functor into endofunctors: [[natural transformation]]s — in particular [[parametric polymorphism|polymorphic]] functions such as <code>reverse</code> — correspond exactly to container morphisms, and are thereby determined by a first-order action on shapes and positions.<ref name='categories-of-containers'>{{cite conference |author1=Michael Abbott |author2=Thorsten Altenkirch |author3=Neil Ghani |year=2003 |title=Categories of Containers |book-title=Foundations of Software Science and Computation Structures (FoSSaCS 2003) |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=2620 |publisher=Springer |pages=23–38 |doi=10.1007/3-540-36576-1_2}}</ref><ref name='containers'/>

Containers are closed under sums, products, composition, and least and greatest [[Fixed point (mathematics)|fixed points]]. The [[initial algebra]] of the extension of <math>S \triangleleft P</math> is the W-type (type of wellfounded trees) <math>\mathsf{W}_{s:S}\,P\,s</math> of [[intuitionistic type theory|Martin-Löf type theory]], so every strictly positive type — including nested inductive types — is the extension of a container.<ref name='containers'/><ref name='nested-w-types'>{{cite conference |author1=Michael Abbott |author2=Thorsten Altenkirch |author3=Neil Ghani |year=2004 |title=Representing Nested Inductive Types Using W-Types |book-title=Automata, Languages and Programming (ICALP 2004) |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=3142 |publisher=Springer |pages=59–71 |doi=10.1007/978-3-540-27836-8_8}}</ref> Over the category of sets, extensions of containers coincide with the one-variable [[Polynomial functor (type theory)|polynomial functors]], and the theory can be developed in any [[locally cartesian closed category]] with W-types in the categorical sense of Moerdijk and Palmgren.<ref name='wellfounded-trees'>{{cite journal |author1=Ieke Moerdijk |author2=Erik Palmgren |year=2000 |title=Wellfounded trees in categories |journal=Annals of Pure and Applied Logic |volume=104 |issue=1–3 |pages=189–218 |doi=10.1016/S0168-0072(00)00012-9}}</ref><ref name='dependent-polynomial'>{{cite conference |author1=Nicola Gambino |author2=Martin Hyland |year=2004 |title=Wellfounded Trees and Dependent Polynomial Functors |book-title=Types for Proofs and Programs (TYPES 2003) |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=3085 |publisher=Springer |pages=210–225 |doi=10.1007/978-3-540-24849-1_14}}</ref><ref name='polynomial-monads'>{{cite journal |author1=Nicola Gambino |author2=Joachim Kock |year=2013 |title=Polynomial functors and polynomial monads |journal=Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society |volume=154 |issue=1 |pages=153–192 |doi=10.1017/S0305004112000394|arxiv=0906.4931 }}</ref>

Containers also admit a formal derivative, whose shapes are shapes with one distinguished position (a "one-hole context"); it obeys laws analogous to those of [[differential calculus]] and underlies [[Zipper (data structure)|zipper]] structures.<ref name='derivatives'>{{cite journal |author1=Michael Abbott |author2=Thorsten Altenkirch |author3=Conor McBride |author4=Neil Ghani |author-link3=Conor McBride |year=2005 |title=∂ for data: Differentiating data structures |journal=Fundamenta Informaticae |volume=65 |issue=1–2 |pages=1–28}}</ref> The containers whose extension carries a [[Monad (category theory)|comonad]] structure are exactly the ''directed containers'', such as nonempty lists, where the comonadic structure is given by taking suffixes.<ref name='directed-containers'>{{cite journal |author1=Danel Ahman |author2=James Chapman |author3=Tarmo Uustalu |year=2014 |title=When Is a Container a Comonad? |journal=Logical Methods in Computer Science |volume=10 |issue=3:14 |doi=10.2168/LMCS-10(3:14)2014 |doi-access=free|arxiv=1408.5809 }}</ref>

== Indexed containers ==
{{Expand section|date=October 2008}}
'''Indexed containers''' (also known as '''dependent polynomial functors''') are a generalisation of containers, which can represent a wider class of types, such as vectors (sized lists).<ref name='indexed-containers'>{{cite web
| author         = Thorsten Altenkirch, Neil Ghani, Peter Hancock, [[Conor McBride]], and Peter Morris
| title          = Indexed Containers
| type        = Unpublished manuscript
| url            = http://strictlypositive.org/indexed-containers.pdf
| accessdate     = 2008-10-30
}}
</ref>

The element type (called the ''input type'') is indexed by shape and position, so it can vary by shape and position, and the extension (called the ''output type'') is also indexed by shape.
